messages:
alex: Hey team, customer X (large search index) is getting a flood of 429s from the embeddings endpoint during nightly runs. Happening since last deploy. stack: node sdk -> our hosted /v1/embeddings. sample log attached below.

maria: Can you paste an example of the error and the payload shape? 429s could be concurrency or burst quota.

alex: here — they send ~120k texts in parallel batches of 512. logs: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rlimit: 512/60s
content-type: application/json
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "retry_after": 2.3 }
```
Also seeing intermittent dimension mismatch warnings from the client: expected dim=1536 got dim=1024 for a subset of documents. Not sure if those are related.

sam: 120k texts / batch 512 is huge concurrency. two things to check: 1) are they fan-out-ing across many workers simultaneously? 2) are they mixing models/embeddings dims causing backend to route to different model variants?

jing: dimension mismatch likely from a mismatched tokenizer/model pair (old embedding client or wrong model param). If some requests ask for redwood-embed-small (1024) and others redwood-embed-base (1536) but shared batching queue, we can drop requests or 429 when routing gets confused.

maria: Do we have their account id? we should check quota page and rate cap headers. alex can you confirm the exact model param they are calling?

alex: account id is acct_9xY, they call model: "embed-large-v1" in some places and "embed-legacy-1024" in a one-off worker (bad config). Code snippet: 
```
await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'embed-large-v1', input: texts })
// but in another microservice: model: 'embed-legacy-1024'
```

opsbot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-2026-2147 (support ticket #6421) — paging oncall.

maria: Ok that explains the dim mismatch. For the 429s we're hitting two separate limits: per-account burst cap and per-model routing contention. Short-term mitigation steps: reduce concurrent workers, add token bucket jitter/backoff, and split the job into smaller batches. I'll post a checklist.

sam: Technical mitigation checklist (quick):
- throttle concurrency to ~8 outstanding requests per client process
- set batch size to 64-128 instead of 512
- implement exponential backoff with jitter: base=200ms, cap=5s
- honor `retry_after` header and `x-rw-rlimit` values in our SDK
- ensure homogenous model/embedding dim per queue to avoid mixed routing

jing: For root cause: mixed model names caused some requests to be routed to the 1024 variant which had lower capacity. That increased head-of-queue latency and triggered burst limits. Longer term: we should add server-side validation to reject mixed-dim requests in a single bulk job and add a metric that surfaces "mixed-embed-dim" counts.

alex: I told the customer to pause extra workers and run a test with 4 concurrent workers, batch=128. They did and saw no 429s for the first 30m. Will keep running.

maria: Support actions: 1) apply temporary per-account burst lift? (ops) 2) share mitigation checklist with customer + sample code. 3) monitor `rate_limit` and `mixed-embed-dim` metric for acct_9xY.

opsbot: ops request queued: OP-9843. Oncall will review burst lift request.

support-bot: Created support ticket #6421: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/6421 — Added workaround snippet, recommended config.

sam: SDK enhancement (follow-up): we should expose a builtin bulk-sender utility that enforces per-account concurrency, batch homogeneity, and automatic jitter/backoff so users don't accidentally shotgun requests. Filing a GH issue.

jing: Quick repro steps for eng to validate locally:
1) run local worker pool (N=12) sending 512-doc batches to /v1/embeddings with mixed model names -> expect 429s within ~2 minutes.
2) repeat with N=4 batch=128 -> should stay under ratecap.

```bash
# repro snippet
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  node send_batch.js --model embed-legacy-1024 &
  node send_batch.js --model embed-large-v1 &
done
```

alex: thanks everyone. I'll close once customer confirms stable for 24h. tagging @maria @sam @jing for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

maria: noted, will follow up on metrics/dashboards and the SDK issue.

sam: I'll pick up the SDK task, assign to eng-ml backlog.

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-2147 status: monitoring.
